approach: Root cause: the check stage keeps a baseline of failures on the base commit (`is_pre_existing`, `failure_split`, verify.rs:203-222), but nothing maps the file paths a failing check reports to the paths the job changed, and nothing tells the verdict or the verifier how the failure got past the baseline. Fix at those two inputs, with no refusal rule (the verdict is unchanged; share of newly refused readings 0%). (1) verify.rs gets a pure `failure_paths(check, changed_paths, tree_paths)`. It pulls path-like tokens out of a failed check's `output_tail`, keeps only tokens that name a file tracked at the base or the candidate (exact match first; a crate-relative `a/b.rs` resolves by suffix only when exactly one tracked file matches, otherwise it is listed as ambiguous and never called touched), and splits them into touched, untouched and ambiguous. No extension allow-list. (2) `failure_path_finding(check, baseline, changed_paths, tree_paths)` turns that into one Minor Athena finding that also states the route facts the code can read: whether a usable baseline existed (None, a baseline with a note, no entry for the check), whether the same check passed or failed on the base, whether the result was reused from the CI run, and that the check ran on the candidate (the base plus the job's change). The wording never names a cause the run rules out and says plainly that a cited path is where a test panicked or a file its message names, not proof of cause. (3) `judge` pushes it for each blocking check (a failed check that is not pre-existing). `VerdictInputs` gets one field, `tree_paths: &[String]`; empty means unknown and no finding. (4) `verification_stage` reads the tracked paths of the base and the candidate from the verifier snapshot (`ls_tree` of HEAD~1 and HEAD), computes `changed_paths` before the verifier inputs are built, and `verifier_check_views` appends the same finding text to the `detail` of each blocking failed check, which the brief already prints (briefs.rs:1449-1461). Why the route facts: the tested tree is always the base plus the diff. The baseline is taken on `ctx.prediction` (checks.rs:743) and used only when it equals the job's base (verification.rs:51-54); the checks run in a snapshot of base and candidate (verification.rs:2002-2003); a CI result is for the candidate commit (routing.rs:238-242; ci.yml:93 checks out the PR head SHA, not a merge ref). A failure absent from a usable baseline therefore comes from the diff, from the base's tool configuration (toolconfig.rs:73), or from the environment, never from a later merge into the tested tree. The jobs' records are not in the snapshot, so the route each of wcwy, a5sf and 6wfq took cannot be read; the finding records it for the next job. D186 and the CHANGELOG correct the earlier changelog note (CHANGELOG.md:1652-1653) that calls this a clash with a concurrent change.

decisions.choice: Give the verdict and the verifier brief a finding that links the failing output's tracked paths to the job's changed paths and states the baseline route; add no refusal rule.
decisions.reason: The failing stage lacked the link. `judge` has `changed_paths` (verify.rs:167) but never compared them with the output, and the verifier is shown no output for a locally run failing check (`check_result_view` fills the tail only when `r.reused`, verify.rs:75-86). Giving information can prevent the failure, so no refusal is allowed. The finding is Minor, so `serious` (verify.rs:652-655), the reasons and the verdict are unchanged: 0% of past accepted readings newly refused.

rejected.option: Rerun the failing test on the base tree and mark it pre-existing, as the introspections propose
rejected.why: A per-test baseline already exists (verify.rs:203-211). The tested tree is base plus diff, so a base rerun gives the same answer as the baseline. It also needs a new run stage and snapshot.

rejected.option: Excuse or downgrade a failure whose cited paths the job did not change
rejected.why: A new verdict rule that changes what passes. A panic site is the assertion's file, not the cause, so a job that breaks a test it did not edit would be excused. The request asks for information.

rejected.option: Add a field to CheckResultView and render it in crates/athena-context/src/briefs.rs
rejected.why: The existing `detail` is already printed for every check (briefs.rs:1449-1461); a new field touches a second crate and its brief-shape tests for no gain.

rejected.option: Add the paths to CheckRun or the stored check records
rejected.why: CheckRun is a stored record type (athena-data records.rs:868); changing it risks old-record parsing. The paths are derived from `output_tail` when needed.

decisions.choice: Name no cause. The evidence states the baseline route (reused CI result; no usable baseline; baseline with a note; no entry for the check; same check passed on the base; same check failed on the base with other tests), says the check ran on the candidate, and says a cited path does not show what caused the failure.
decisions.reason: Critic findings 1 and 2. When a usable baseline exists the tested tree cannot hold a later merge, so 'may come from a change merged after the base' was wrong. A failure absent from the baseline came from the diff, the base tool configuration or the environment. Panic locations name the asserting file, so the text says so instead of implying a cause. The route is the part that separates cases, and it is read from `inputs.baseline` and `check.reused` (records.rs:888-892; checks.rs:308-337 sets `reused` for any CI-derived record).

rejected.option: Keep 'may come from the base or from a change merged after it'
rejected.why: The code rules it out for a usable baseline and for a CI result (ci.yml:93, routing.rs:238-242).

rejected.option: Treat every cited path the job did not change as evidence the job is not at fault
rejected.why: A test can fail on a file the job did not touch because of what the job changed. The finding reports facts and the check still fails the verdict.

decisions.choice: Resolve cited tokens against the tracked files of the base and the candidate, passed in as `tree_paths`. No extension allow-list and no blind suffix match.
decisions.reason: Critic finding 3. Athena runs on other repositories, so `.py`, `.go` and `.ts` paths must work. A token counts only when it names a tracked file: exact match first; a token containing `/` may match by suffix, one match resolves, several are listed as ambiguous (a failure in crate b citing `src/lib.rs` is never called touched because crate a changed its own). Bare names without `/` match exactly or not at all. Targets, `..`, URLs, durations and test names are dropped because they are not tracked. A cap of 10 listed paths and 400 examined tokens bounds the cost. `vsnap` already holds both commits (verification.rs:398-406) and `Git::ls_tree` exists (athena-git lib.rs:516).

rejected.option: A hard-coded extension allow-list with a suffix match on changed paths
rejected.why: Drops other languages silently and marks a path as touched when another crate's file shares a suffix.
They were written for verifier findings: `path_of_token` strips one trailing `:digits`, so `file.rs:12:5:` keeps `:5:`, and `looks_like_path` accepts any dotted token.

decisions.choice: Make no claim when `changed_paths` or `tree_paths` is empty, when no tracked path is cited, or when the check passed or is pre-existing.
decisions.reason: An empty changed list means unknown (verify.rs:164-167); an empty tree list means the snapshot could not be read. The existing assertion `judge_against(None, &[check(false)]).findings.is_empty()` (verify.rs:2774) keeps holding.

rejected.option: Treat an empty list as 'the job changed nothing'
rejected.why: A job with an empty diff fails earlier (system facts: empty producer diff), so an empty list in `judge` means no data.

decisions.choice: Leave the new finding in the lists a retry carries, and pin that with a test. Do not add it to `must_address`.
decisions.reason: Critic finding 4. `carry` (retry.rs:714-732) copies every finding of every severity, then the failed check's output tail, into the retry reader's brief (briefs/reader.rs:472-483, shown as quoted data). The existing Minor 'newly failing' finding goes there the same way, and the new text sits beside the output it derives from and claims no cause. `tree_retry_seed` (retry.rs:416-443) never sees it: `qualifies_for_tree_retry` needs every check to have passed (retry.rs:347-348). `finding_blocks` (verify.rs:688-690) keeps it out of `must_address` and `finding_is_content_only`.

rejected.why: A special case in the retry path with no reason beyond the worry; the owner and the retrying reader gain from seeing the route facts next to the failed output.

decisions.choice: Leave crates/athena-core/src/run/checks.rs unchanged although the brief lists it.
decisions.reason: `take_baseline`, `baseline_for` and the in-loop check (checks.rs:272, 446, 735) record and compare everything the finding reads (`Baseline.note`, per-check `passed`, `failed_tests`, `reused_from`). The gap is in the verdict inputs and the brief, so a checks.rs edit would have no demonstration.

rejected.option: Record in the baseline why it was unusable (never taken, or taken on another commit)
rejected.why: `judge` receives only the usable baseline; the finding says 'no usable baseline' for both. The distinction would change a stored record for no gain in the verdict or the brief.

It returns the empty result when `check.passed`, or `changed_paths` or `tree_paths` is empty. Otherwise it splits `output_tail` on whitespace and on `()[]{}<>,;'"`=|`, strips a leading `./`, cuts at the first `:`, trims a trailing `.`, and keeps a token only if it is non-empty, has a `.`, has no `..` segment, does not start with `/` or `~` and uses only [A-Za-z0-9_./-]. It resolves a token to a tracked file: exact match in a `HashSet<&str>` of `tree_paths`; else, only when the token contains `/`, the tracked files ending with `/<token>`: one resolves, two or more go to `ambiguous` (the token, never touched or untouched). It dedupes by order of first appearance, stops at MAX_CITED_PATHS listed paths and MAX_CITED_TOKENS examined tokens, and puts a resolved path in `touched` when it equals an entry of `changed_paths`, else in `untouched`.

(with '(read from the CI run {address})' when `reused_from` is set); an entry that failed -> 'The same check failed on the base commit too, but not with these tests.'; no entry -> 'The baseline holds no result for this check.'. risks.risk: A cited path outside the job's change does not show the job did not cause the failure (a test can read a file the job's code broke), and a panic site names the asserting file. The finding could mislead the verifier or the owner.
risks.mitigation: The evidence says a cited path is where a test panicked or a file its message names and does not show the cause; it names no cause; the check still fails the verdict; the finding is Minor. The route sentence is the part that separates cases. D186 and the CHANGELOG state the limit.

risks.risk: Token extraction picks a tracked file by accident (a bare `Cargo.toml` or `lib.rs` in prose) or misses a form (Windows paths, a path with spaces).
risks.mitigation: Only tracked files count; bare names match exactly or not at all; a crate-relative token with several matches is ambiguous and never claimed touched or untouched. A missed form gives no finding, which is today's behavior. The table-driven test pins the forms.

risks.risk: Only the last 200 lines of a failed run's output are kept (`FAILED_TAIL_LINES`, checks.rs:186), so the panic or message line may be cut and no path is found.
risks.mitigation: No path gives no finding and changes nothing. The limit is recorded in D186. Stored output sizes belong to `failure_section`, which is another change.

risks.risk: `ls_tree` of two commits on every job adds a git call and memory for the tracked paths of a large repository.
risks.mitigation: `git ls-tree -r` of two commits in a local snapshot is cheap next to the checks that just ran; the list is built once per verification stage and an error gives an empty list and no finding. The token scan is capped at 400 distinct tokens and 10 listed paths.

risks.risk: Adding a field to `VerdictInputs` breaks a literal I did not find.
risks.mitigation: I searched the repository for `VerdictInputs {` and found ten sites (one production, one in send_back.rs tests, eight in verify.rs tests); each is updated, and the compiler would flag any other.

risks.risk: Moving the `changed_paths` computation above the verifier inputs changes borrows of `closing.candidate`.
risks.mitigation: It is a plain clone into a `Vec<String>` from the same expression as today (verification.rs:409-413); the compiler and existing tests would catch an error.

risks.risk: The whole-job test depends on the fixture check failing only after the producer's edit and on the baseline passing.
risks.mitigation: It uses the same pattern as `NEEDS_FIXED_FILE` (tests.rs:4500): `grep -q 'A demo' README.md || exit 0` passes on the base README `# Demo` and fails after the edit `A demo.` (tests.rs:259). It asserts the Rejected state and the baseline sentence, so a wrong fixture fails loudly.
